data.headline: Tariff for KEL consumers raised by PKR 0.40 per unit:
data.summary: NEPRA has increased power tariff up to PKR 0.40 per unit for the consumers of KEL.

data.headline: KEL willing to refund PKR 247mn to its clients:
data.summary: KEL, the Karachi-based power utility, has filed a petition with NEPRA willing to refund PKR 0.16 per unit to consumers as part of monthly FCA for September 2024, totaling approximately PKR 247mn.

data.headline: NEPRA approves generation tariff for KEL:
data.summary: NEPRA has approved generation tariff of KEL post June 30, 2023, along with dissenting decision of Member (Finance and Tariff). The tariff control period shall be 7 years or remaining useful life, whichever is lower except for BQPS-III which shall be 11 years.

data.headline: Minimum tax payment: KEL’s fuel cost, subsidy recoveries should be treated as turnover SHC:
data.summary: SHC ruled that the subsidy and fuel cost recovered by KEL from consumers has to be treated as turnover for the purpose of minimum tax payment under Section 113 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001.

data.headline: Covid subsidy to consumers NA body summons KEL CEO over non-payment:
data.summary: The NA’s standing committee on industries and production has summoned the KEL CEO over non-payment of corona subsidy to Karachi power consumers.

data.headline: KEL seeks to extract PKR 853mn more for Aug:
data.summary: KEL sought a 51-paisa per unit additional fuel adjustment for August to collect about PKR 853mn more from its consumers in the billing month of October. The move contrasts with a proposed 57-paisa per unit refund for the same month by public sector distribution companies (Discos).

data.headline: Q4FY24 adjustment Tariffs of Discos, KEL raised by PKR 1.74/unit:
data.summary: NEPRA has increased tariffs of Discos and KEL by PKR 1.74 per unit to recover additional amount of PKR 43.23bn from consumers for fourth quarter of FY24 to be recovered in the bills of September to November 2024.

data.headline: NEPRA fines KEL PKR 1mn for safety lapse:
data.summary: The country's power regulator has slapped a fine of PKR 10mn on KEL —the power utility that supplies electricity to Karachi—for "lack of safety measures/culture" which resulted in the death of a person within its service territory during FY23.
